name: DEAD-box helicase 41

function.text: DDX41 encodes a DEAD-box helicase-family protein implicated in RNA processing and cellular nucleic-acid sensing.

germline.text: Strong or definitive GenCC assertions link constitutional variants to DDX41-related hematologic malignancy predisposition syndrome (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Acquired DDX41 mutations occur in myeloid neoplasms, including myelodysplastic neoplasms and acute myeloid leukemia, and may coexist with an inherited predisposing allele. Tumor-only testing cannot establish the constitutional origin of a finding.

function.text: DDX41 encodes a DEAD-box helicase-family protein implicated in RNA processing and cellular nucleic-acid sensing. Based in part on similarity, it plays pivotal roles in innate immune sensing and hematopoietic homeostasis. It modulates the homeostasis of dsDNA through its ATP-dependent DNA-unwinding activity and ATP-independent strand-annealing activity. It selectively modulates the transcription of certain immunity-associated genes by regulating their alternative splicing.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with DDX41-related hematologic malignancy predisposition syndrome (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Acquired DDX41 mutations occur in myeloid neoplasms, including myelodysplastic neoplasms and acute myeloid leukemia, and may coexist with an inherited predisposing allele.
